transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-10-03 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Diego Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM); Maya Rios (Ironclad CTO), Samir Khan (Infra Lead), Lena Ortiz (SRE), Owen Park (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in focused on contract extension options, pushing Ironclad onto additional edge regions (us-west-2 then eu-west-1), and a short 24-hour benchmark to validate latency and cost for their burst patterns. Customer reiterated need for private VPC option for sensitive manifests and asked clarifying questions on audit logs, KMS and model fallbacks.

Topics Covered:
- Current usage patterns and upcoming spike forecast (Black Friday prep)
- Dedicated capacity vs hosted + burst; unit economics
- Multi-region onboarding sequence and data residency
- Security/compliance (SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs)
- 24-hour benchmark plan and success criteria

Action items (brief): see action_items field above

Transcript body:
00:00:05 Ava Martinez (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. quick check — is everyone seeing my screen?
00:00:14 Maya Rios (CTO): yep, we can see it. thanks ava. running a little tight today so we flagged the key things up front — renewal numbers, regions, and that weekend spike plan.
00:00:27 Diego Chen (SE): perfect. i'll be focused on perf numbers and the benchmark. quick intro — i'm diego on the se side, will run the 24-hour run with your dev traffic and validate both latency and p50/p99.
00:00:40 Samir Khan (Infra): great. to set expectations, our infra team cares mostly about p99 tail and cold start for kv cache, and also the cost per 1k tokens because we have a mix of short chat and long render prompts.
00:00:56 Ava Martinez (AE): totally — thanks samir. today we want to outline two renewal options: 1) standard reserved capacity with predictable throughput; 2) tiered reserved + burst model where you pay a lower committed rate and have burst credits. i'll send numbers after the call.
00:01:12 Owen Park (Procurement): one note from procurement — any changes to data retention or egress could affect our contracts. we need clear language about where customer data lives and logs.
00:01:23 Priya Patel (CSM): we'll include a data residency addendum for regions and clarify retention windows; also we have the security-pack.pdf that summarizes SOC2, encryption, and logging.
00:01:34 Lena Ortiz (SRE): can you run through the private deployment option briefly? our compliance team is leaning toward V-P-C, and we want to understand the onboarding window.
00:01:45 Diego Chen (SE): sure. Redwood Private can be provisioned into your VPC; it includes a private control plane plus customer-managed subnets. onboarding typically 4-6 weeks for eu-onprem parity, but for a VPC-based private we can aim for 2-3 weeks if there's a dedicated infra contact and cleared network peering.
00:02:05 Maya Rios (CTO): 2-3 weeks would be ideal. what about keys — we use an HSM-backed k... k-m-s solution, need to ensure CMEK support?
00:02:14 Diego Chen (SE): yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. some early setups require a short key rotation policy alignment, but it's supported. sorry there was a slight mis-typing earlier in our doc where it read 'K-V cash' — it's KV cache, just to be clear.
00:02:30 Samir Khan: ha, ok. another concern — model fallbacks. if you run out of capacity in a region, does Redwood auto-failover to a cheaper/smaller model and how transparent is that?
00:02:40 Ava Martinez: good question. we have routing policies — you can set priority by latency or cost. default behavior is to fall back to a compatible variant (e.g., quantized) with a header that indicates fallback occurred. we'll show sample traces in the rollout docs.
00:02:58 Maya Rios: will that change response shapes? our downstream validators are strict.
00:03:05 Diego Chen: generally no — same output schema, but there can be slight quality regression; we'll include eval metrics from previous rollouts so you can see token-level changes. also you can configure automatic rollback if quality drops against your prompt set.
00:03:22 Owen Park: procurement asks for SLA language — what uptime and latency SLAs do you offer for Dedicated vs Hosted?
00:03:30 Ava Martinez: Dedicated comes with an SLA for throughput and availability; hosted has best-effort SLAs for free tier but paid tiers and dedicated include formal SLA. i'll include sample SLA clauses in the quote.
00:03:44 Maya Rios: one of our blockers is Black Friday prep — we expect a 6x burst in concurrent requests for two 48-hour windows. how does the burst credit model work in practice?
00:03:57 Priya Patel: burst credits let you exceed committed baseline for short windows, billed at a lower incremental rate than on-demand. the SE team can model cost for your exact spike pattern during the 24h benchmark.
00:04:12 Diego Chen: for the 24-hour run we'll replay a sample of your dev traffic capturing concurrency, token distribution, and prompt lengths. we'll generate p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens. note — if you want exact Black Friday sim, we should schedule a separate stress window.
00:04:30 Samir Khan: yeah can do. we'll provide a sanitized traffic sample — nothing PII — but has representative prompt mix.
00:04:37 Maya Rios: sending that after this call.
00:04:40 Ava Martinez: great. quick question on regions — you mentioned us-west-2 first, then eu-west-1, any need for apac immediately?
00:04:48 Maya Rios: not immediately; APAC might be Q2 2028. priority is US then EU to satisfy our European customers' data residency.
00:04:57 Diego Chen: ok we'll provide a staged activation plan: boot us-west-2 first with cache warmers, then eu-west-1 with snapshot replication. expected time between region activations is ~7-10 days for reserved capacity, faster for hosted routing only.
00:05:14 Lena Ortiz: snapshot replication — does that mean copying KV caches or model artifacts? we don't want proprietary manifests leaving our control.
00:05:22 Diego Chen: good clarification — we replicate model weights/artifacts from Redwood's model catalog where allowed; customer-specific KV caches (prefixes) remain in your VPC when using private deployment. for hosted, prefix caching may be stored on Redwood's infra but encrypted at rest; we'll mark PII-sensitive prefixes and exclude them.
00:05:43 Owen Park: procurement — any penalties for early termination if we commit to reserved and need to downscope?
00:05:51 Ava Martinez: standard reserved contracts have break clauses; we can build in a 60-day notice with a prorated invoice. i'll surface two contract templates — one flexible and one with steeper discounts.
00:06:03 Maya Rios: on security pack — can you confirm audit log retention options? our auditors want seven years for access logs.
00:06:12 Priya Patel: we can extend audit log retention as an add-on. default is 1 year in the hosted plan, but enterprise add-on covers longer retention plus export to a customer S3 bucket.
00:06:22 Samir Khan: will exports include raw request bodies? that's sensitive.
00:06:27 Diego Chen: exports can be filtered — we'll exclude full prompt bodies if needed and only include metadata and redaction markers. that will be part of the security-pack.pdf and the SOC2 attestation.
00:06:40 Maya Rios: great. curious about cost delta — if we use private VPC with dedicated capacity vs hosted reserved, what's ballpark?
00:06:48 Ava Martinez: privately managed dedicated typically carries an infra premium — roughly 15-25% on top of equivalent hosted reserved, depending on region and redundancy. we can give you exact numbers in the quote; that's one of the items i'll send.
00:07:02 Owen Park: we might accept that for compliance.
00:07:06 Diego Chen: also you can compress costs with quantization profiles for non-critical prompts; Redwood Optimize gives model/quant recommendations by workload to reduce unit cost while keeping quality. we'll include suggested profiles from past customers.
00:07:21 Lena Ortiz: do those quant profiles require model changes that affect latency?
00:07:26 Diego Chen: they can improve throughput but may slightly increase p99 due to decompression on some stacks; the tradeoff usually favors cost with minor latency shift. benchmark will show that.
00:07:40 Maya Rios: okay. i want a short recap — what will you run and what decisions do we need to make?
00:07:47 Ava Martinez: recap: Redwood runs a 24-hour benchmark on your dev traffic (diego), Redwood sends two renewal package options (ava) — standard and tiered burst (due 10-07), we'll share security pack and contract templates (priya), and customer confirms region order and stakeholder list (maya) by 10-08.
00:08:07 Owen Park: procurement also wants a copy of sample SLA clauses and termination language.
00:08:12 Ava Martinez: noted — will include.
00:08:16 Maya Rios: sounds good. couple of quick clarifying q's from the team — 1) telemetry: will we get token-level cost breakdowns per route? 2) can we do canary rollouts across regions?
00:08:29 Diego Chen: yes to both. Console provides token-level breakdown and per-route dashboards; and rollouts support canaries and automated rollback tied to your eval set.
00:08:39 Samir Khan: any gotchas for network peering? we have a forced proxy for egress in our VPC.
00:08:46 Priya Patel: we often see customers with egress proxies; we can either peer via private link or accommodate proxy routes with a short firewall rule window for provisioning. SE will document the exact ports.
00:08:58 Maya Rios: ok that helps.
00:09:02 Ava Martinez: we'll put the provisioning runbook in the onboarding checklist. that'll include port list, IAM roles, and sample terraform snippets.
00:09:10 Diego Chen: i'll add a note about KV cache warmers and build a script to pre-warm top prefixes so your p99 cold starts don't spike during Black Friday.
00:09:20 Lena Ortiz: excellent. one last ask — can we see a demo of the console traces for a fallback event? we want to show execs how graceful degradation looks.
00:09:30 Ava Martinez: yes, we can prepare a short 15-min console demo in the next call.
00:09:36 Maya Rios: let's schedule that.
00:09:40 Ava Martinez: any final procurement red flags?
00:09:44 Owen Park: nothing new, just timeline alignment — procurement needs the final quote to start internal approvals, so the 10-07 deliverable is critical.
00:09:53 Ava Martinez: understood. okay we'll wrap with the next steps. thanks everyone.
00:10:00 (call continues — diego and lena go deeper into bench config)
00:22:14 Diego Chen: (talking through benchmark spreadsheet) — so we've added concurrency buckets, prompt length distribution, and token histograms. i'll run both quantized and non-quantized variants.
00:35:03 Lena Ortiz: small note — can we keep the raw prompt bodies out of the bench logs?
00:35:10 Diego Chen: yes we're masking prompts in the bench telemetry; we'll only store hashes and metadata.
00:40:05 Maya Rios: thanks team. that covers it from our side. we look forward to the quote.
00:40:12 Ava Martinez: thanks all, next steps noted.

References shared in call:
- capacity-plan.xlsx (uploaded to shared drive)
- security-pack.pdf (link sent to security team)
- renewal-quote-template.docx (to be populated)
- benchmark-results-template.csv (will be filled by SE after run)

Meeting close: 15:52 PDT
